page_title: BBC Learning English - English at Work / Doing it by the book
title: Doing it by the book
topic: Language to use in a health and safety report
description:
Tom has taken a tumble at Tip Top Trading. He was chasing a mouse but he fell over! What a disaster! Will Anna be able to help and find the right phrases to deal with health and safety at work?
This episode focuses on what to say when you need to talk about health and safety at work.
phrases: What was the cause of the accident?
How could the accident have been avoided?

listening_challenge.question: In the accident, what did Tom trip over?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Welcome back to the offices of Tip Top Trading where Tom has taken a tumble. He was trying to catch a mouse but tripped over. Can Anna help soothe the pain? Let's find out.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Ooh… oww… ouch. My arm really hurts.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: What's all this noise about?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: It's Tom. He's had an accident – tripped over a mouse – I mean tripped over trying to catch a mouse.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Golly gosh. Are you OK Tom?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: I dunno. I think I've broken something.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Your pencil I think! Just sit there at my desk and I'll go and call a first-aider.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Anna,you're going to have to fill in one of those Health and Safety reports.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh really? Do we have to?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: It's procedure and it's the law – it's got to be done.  Now Tom, would a biscuit make you feel better?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Health and Safety is important in the workplace. The office needs to be a safe place to work in, but accidents do happen and that's when you have to report it. Anna, do you know where to find the form you need to fill in?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I think so. It's here on the company intranet… here it is, 'accident report form'.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Yes, it's sometimes called an 'incident or accident report form'. It will ask you: How did the accident happen? What was the cause of the accident? Were there any injuries? And how could the accident have been avoided?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: OK, I had better get started.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Right, I've call the first-aider. She'll be here in ten minutes. Now, do you need a hand with this form, Anna?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Yes please Denise. It wants to know how the accident happened.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Just say there was a mouse… no, a large rat… running about that needed catching. And Tom, very bravely, tried to catch it

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Yes… and then he tripped over something.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Was it your ego Tom?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Err? Ha ha. Ouch! No, it was a sample box of Perfect Peaches.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: So, the cause of the accident was a box of Perfect Peaches left on the floor. Who left them there anyway?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: That might have been me Denise.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: What do I always say about putting things away? Now Anna, it says here 'Were there any injuries?'

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: So I'll write, 'Yes, a member of staff broke his arm.'

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Sprainedhis arm. I think he'd be in a lot more pain if it was broken, hey Tom?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: What? Err, yeah. It still hurts though.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Hmm! Now finally it says 'What can be done to avoid this accident again?'

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Get rid of the mice… I mean rats?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: No. Store things away properly and keep the office tidy, eh Tom?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Yeah, I suppose so… but I was only trying to catch that mouse.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: I know, very heroic. I'm starting to see what Anna sees in you, you know.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Oh no, Anna, our dinner date!

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: So, it's been an eventful day in the office. Anna has done the proper thing by completing an accident report form. If you have to report an accident at work, here are some of the questions you might be asked:
How did the accident happen?
What was the cause of the accident?
Were there any injuries? And:
How could the accident have been avoided?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: So luckily for Anna she might get out of that date with Tom!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Hey Tom, don't look so glum. I'm up for dinner if you still are?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Ouch… really?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Sure Tom, and as you've only got one arm now, you won't be hugging me all the time.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: You'll have to spoon feed him his food too!

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Denise, could you go and call pest control please?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Careful what you say Denise, or you may get injured too! So it looks Anna and Tom's dinner date is on – I can't wait to be a fly-on-the-wall! See you again soon. Bye!
